text:
Alex: Heads up — after the kernel selector change yesterday we're seeing continuous-batching pad waste go up ~22% on P100 pool, and two infra hosts hit OOMs during the 3am soak. Not sure if it's allocator tuning or the KV cache shadowing more pages.

Marta: Yikes. Any repro traces? allocation telemetry or `nvprof` dumps? :eyes:

Alex: Repro: run `make perf-load` on model-c with seq-dist skewed to long tails. Attaching the condensed sample: 
```
Batch sizes: [1,1,2,4,8,8,16] -> growth spikes at step 4
Pad overhead per batch: +45KB/seq on average after kernel switch
OOM log: cudaMalloc failed at workspace_alloc +0x3ac
```

Jem: Can you paste the allocator watermarks? I want to see slab fragmentation numbers and whether the slow kernel uses larger temp buffers.

Alex: Watermarks: 
`slab_total: 48GB, slab_free: 2.1GB, slab_frag: 4.7GB estimated`
Kernel switch metadata: new kernel requests `workspace_bytes_hint=1.4x` vs old `1.0x` for same seq len.

Dinesh: That 1.4x bump smells like kernel allocating per-layer scratch rather than reusing a pooled buffer. If so we should patch it to call `reuse_workspace_if_possible()` before fallback.

Kai: Also check KV cache shadowing — I remember a regression where the KV cache started duplicating prefix pages during concurrent batch growth. That doubles per-seq overhead for chat-like workloads.

perf-bot: Profiling report generated: https://perf-reports.internal/2351112223 — shows a 28% increase in peak workspace per-request and a 15% increase in avg allocation calls per forward.

Marta: Thanks @perf-bot. From the trace it looks like `kernel_fast_attention` opted into `per_head_scratch` path which allocs an extra buffer per batch item when batch sizes vary. The continuous batcher sends mixed sequence lengths which triggers repeated resize ops.

Jem: Two actionable hypotheses: 1) kernel path needs to reuse a single scratch across the batch (amortize per-seq) 2) allocator tunables should favor coalescing small freelist entries to avoid fragmentation on mixed sizes.

Alex: For (1) I tried a local patch to hoist scratch allocation outside the per-seq loop and it reduced peak workspace by ~35% in my run. Patch: 
```c++
// before: for (item : batch) allocate scratch
// after: auto scratch = pool.acquire(max_scratch_needed); for (item : batch) use(scratch);
```

Dinesh: Nice. For (2) we can try lowering `mini_slab_threshold` from 64KB -> 32KB so small allocations get grouped, and increase `coalesce_window_ms` to 10ms to let batching combine ephemeral frees. That should reduce slab_frag.

Kai: We should also add a guard in smart-routing: avoid switching to the higher-scratch kernel when expected batch entropy (stddev(seq_len)) > threshold. Fallback to stable kernel. Could be a quick mitigation.

Marta: Agreed. Short-term plan: 1) revert kernel selector override (if any) and add entropy check, 2) land reuse hoist patch, 3) tweak allocator mini_slab. I'll open PRs.

Jem: Also add a small kv-cache metric: `kv_shadow_pages_per_request`. If it spikes during mixed batches we can link it to pad growth.

perf-bot: Canary alert created: dedicated-pool-3, rule `workspace_peak > 40GB` with note "rollback candidate".

Alex: Running targeted canary now with the hoist patch and `mini_slab_threshold=32KB`. Will report numbers in ~20 mins.

Dinesh: If hoist + slab tweak doesn't fix it, we should consider adding a temporary global cap on per-request workspace (soft limit with graceful fallback) to avoid OOM cascades. Not ideal, but avoids customer impact.

Kai: Agreed. Also add a short test in `perf/integration` that simulates continuous batching with long-tail seqs so this doesn't regress again.

Marta: I'll coordinate PRs: kernel hoist (#4821), allocator tune (#4822), routing entropy guard (#4823), kv metric (#4824). Tagging @Jem for review on allocator changes. :pray:

Alex: Canary result: peak workspace down 30%, slab_free recovered ~1.8GB, no OOMs in 30m. Preliminary win for hoist + slab tweak.

Jem: Great. After merges let's run a 24h soak. Also capture perf traces pre/post for release notes.

Marta: I'll keep this thread updated during the soak. Thanks everyone :rocket:
